The primitives form a cascading data pipeline: packets capture the current state, placeholder stubs ensure forward compatibility during data gaps, indicators provide lead-time insights, and lint mechanisms enforce quality gates. This architecture mirrors GSI's Bayesian updating framework, where uncertainty is managed through conservative priors (placeholders) and verified through sequential testing (lint). The key mathematical unification lies in treating data availability as a stochastic process, allowing for robust decision-making even when individual components are missing. Failure modes include premature activation of stubbed values leading to false confidence and overly aggressive lint policies causing unnecessary delays. The cross-layer veto condition ensures that placeholder values do not leak into production without proper verification, maintaining anti-collinearity between development and operational environments.
